The comment highlighted in figure 3.1 justifies the use of another deprecated function, get_recent_blockhash, through the #[allow(deprecated)] attribute, but the comment does not justify the use of calculate_fee. As a result, developers could overlook this deprecated function.
candidates.exclusion_note: solana/bridge/client/src/main.rs still calls calculate_fee on the default branch (6c4aad86 replaced a different deprecated call in nft_bridge), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 3. Use of deprecated methods

candidates.description: In several places, the code panics when an arithmetic overflow or underflow occurs. Panics should be reserved for programmer errors (e.g., assertion violations). Panicking on user errors dilutes the utility of the panic operation.
candidates.title: 4. Use of panics on invalid inputs

candidates.description: Type cosplay is when a contract account of one type is passed in as another type, resulting in type confusion. The bridge contract protects against this issue in certain special cases but has no general protection.
candidates.exclusion_note: Trail of Bits did no fix review; no commit referencing the finding or its public issue was found (git log --grep for TOB/issue numbers, history of solana/ and cosmwasm/ since July 2022), and the cited code is unchanged on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 5. No general protection against type cosplay in bridge

candidates.description: The Solana contracts’ documentation is insufficient, lacking high-level descriptions and examples. Insufficient documentation makes the code difficult to review and increases the risk that developers attempting to integrate their projects with Wormhole will make mistakes.
candidates.exclusion_note: Trail of Bits did no fix review; no commit referencing the finding or its public issue was found (git log --grep for TOB/issue numbers, history of solana/ and cosmwasm/ since July 2022), and the cited code is unchanged on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 6. Insufficient documentation of Solana contracts

candidates.description: Trail of Bits used cargo outdated to detect outdated dependencies in the Wormhole codebase. The tool detected a number of outdated packages that are referenced by the Cargo.toml files.
candidates.exclusion_note: No commit updates the listed crates to their latest versions as recommended (18eac4e3 bumped the Solana SDK only to 1.10.31 during the audit), so no fix commit could be named.
candidates.title: 7. Outdated dependencies

candidates.description: Accounts that are not modified by the Solana contracts are specified as writable by the AccountMeta::new constructor. Since the accounts are not modified, AccountMeta::new_readonly could be used instead.
candidates.exclusion_note: solana/modules/nft_bridge/program/src/instructions.rs still uses AccountMeta::new for the rent sysvar on the default branch (issue 1533 named in the report), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 8. AccountMeta::new constructor used for non-writable accounts

candidates.description: The cw20-wrapped package’s tests do not build. The issue appears to be a change to the mock_dependencies function in the cosmwasm_std library. The existing tests try to pass one argument to this function (e.g., figure 9.1). However, beginning with cosmwasm_std 1.0.0, the function takes no arguments (figure 9.2). Since the tests rely on cosmwasm_std 1.0.0, they do not build.
candidates.title: 9. cw20-wrapped tests do not build

candidates.description: In several places, such as the examples in figures 10.1 and 10.2, the cosmwasm token bridge checks for the absence of a key in storage. If an error is returned, the contract implicitly assumes that it is a NotFound error. However, the load method could also return ParseErr (figure 10.3). Thus, the current practice could allow such errors to go unnoticed.
candidates.exclusion_note: The token bridge still treats any load error as NotFound (bucket.load(...).ok() and existing.is_ok() in cosmwasm/contracts/token-bridge/src/contract.rs on the default branch), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 10. CosmWasm token bridge does not distinguish between loading errors

candidates.description: The Solana and CosmWasm Wormhole contracts perform fixed point integer division with one decimal of precision (scaling factor of 10) to calculate a two-thirds quorum.
candidates.exclusion_note: The report cites pull 1536, but no commit of it is on the default branch and both contracts still use the scaled formula (post_vaa.rs, cosmwasm wormhole state.rs); 3a1dd9ec simplified only sdk/rust, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 11. Quorum calculation can be simplified and made more robust

candidates.description: CosmWasm token bridges store the addresses of bridges on other chains. However, once an address is set, it can never be changed. This could be problematic if control of an external bridge is ever lost.
candidates.exclusion_note: Wormhole declined to add the feature (appendix E); handle_register_chain still rejects re-registration, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 12. Bridge contract addresses cannot be updated

candidates.description: The CosmWasm core contract exposes a function, parse_and_verify_vaa, to verify the structure of a given VAA. However, the function also checks that the VAA was not previously processed by the core contract.
candidates.exclusion_note: Wormhole acknowledged the finding without a change (appendix E), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 13. Wormhole archive is checked unnecessarily

candidates.description: The send_native function performs unchecked math that may overflow and cause a 0 (or a sufficiently small value) to be stored in the counter_bucket for a given asset address. Then, if receive_native loads this storage value and subtracts a greater amount, the operation will revert due to the use of checked_sub, which guards against overflows. Transfers of native tokens may be disrupted until a contract upgrade can mitigate this issue.
candidates.exclusion_note: send_native in cosmwasm/contracts/token-bridge/src/state.rs still adds without checked math on the default branch (issue 1541 named in the report), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 14. Overflow of native transfer counters may cause reverts

candidates.description: The CosmWasm contracts use checked math fairly consistently; however, there are several instances in which unchecked math is used without explanation. While only one instance was identified as a vulnerability (TOB-WORM-14), the other instances of unchecked math should use their respective checked math operation unless a justification is documented.
candidates.exclusion_note: The cited unchecked operations (10u128.pow(...), amount + fee, balance subtraction) remain in cosmwasm/contracts/token-bridge/src/contract.rs on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 15. Inconsistent use of checked math

candidates.description: Following a bug report of an uninitialized implementation contract that could be destroyed, a new Wormhole implementation was deployed that deleted the function body of initialize. While deleting the body of initialize mitigated the vulnerability, more robust safeguards against contract destruction should be implemented. The current protections are not documented, and they are not standard practice.
candidates.exclusion_note: No onlyProxy guard exists in ethereum/contracts on the default branch (issue 1539 named in the report; 648b3616 fixes issue 1930, a different initialization issue), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: 16. Insufficient safeguards against destruction in the proxy

candidates.description: We found that when nft-bridge contract is deploying nft-wrapped subcontract, the attacker can set their account as the authority for the newly created subcontract. This is possible because deploying and initialization is not done atomically.
candidates.exclusion_note: The report notes the nft-bridge patch was not verified; near/contracts/nft-bridge on the default branch still deploys and calls new in separate chained promises, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Race-Condition when deploying wrapped-nft contract

candidates.description: In the token-bridge contract we found that an attacker is able to mark a VAA as used without executing its intended action supplied inside the VAA payload. One example of such an action is cross-chain token transfer. Due to the wormhole bridge design, anyone is able to relay signed VAAs from guardians to the token-bridgen contract. This means that by using this method, an attacker can invalidate other users’ VAAs.
candidates.title: Marking token-bridge VAA as used incorrectly

candidates.description: We found that register_emitter function allows anyone to reset their supposedly monotonically increasing sequence number. This means that seq field inside VAA can be reset for any message pub- lisher(on NEAR) by anyone. This breaks the purpose of the seq field inside the published VAAs.
candidates.title: Reset VAA sequence number for any emitter

candidates.description: VAA payloads have specific formats which need to be strictly followed by all the contract implementations on different blockchains. We found that the NEAR contract had several places where it was not correctly following the payload specifications.
candidates.title: Incorrect parsing of VAA payload

candidates.description: update_contract_work does not check storage deposit correctly. Even though the required cost is calculated, the fact that caller did not attach enough deposit is ignored.
candidates.title: No storage deposit checking when upgrading contract

candidates.description: We found that finish_deploy callback which was supposed to be checking whether new ft contract was deployed successfully, was actually checking the status of deposit refund Promise.
candidates.title: Rollback not checking failure of correct promise

candidates.description: In token-bridge vaa_transfer, when handling native NEAR and nfee == 0, the contract fails to refund the user the deposit:
candidates.title: Deposit is not Refunded in Certain Cases in token-bridge vaa_transfer

candidates.description: In token-bridge send_transfer_near, NEAR values are truncated to 8 decimals and remaining dust amounts are retained by the token-bridge contract instead of being refunded.
candidates.title: Fractional NEAR is not Refunded in send_transfer_near

candidates.description: We recommend creating rust structs for each kind of VAA payload and writing serialization and deseri- alization functions for those structs. Encapsulating parsing and packing code into a single place would make it easier to verify and use rather than using offsets all around the codebase. Refactoring would allow developers working on business logic to not have to think about payload offsets.
candidates.exclusion_note: Status TODO in the report; payload parsing in near/contracts still uses offsets on the default branch (git log of near/contracts), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Refactor VAA payload parsing and packing code

candidates.description: We found that function register_account stores AccountIds created from arbitrary strings us- ing AccountId::new_unchecked. This function does not check whether a given string is valid AccountId or not. Even though most unchecked AccountId uses would result in panics, we believe it’s better to make checking explicit.
candidates.title: Unchecked Account Ids

candidates.description: It is a common pattern for NEAR contracts to prevent calling important functions with just FunctionCall keys. For example, such functions include ones that might end up transferring users NFTs or fungible tokens to someone else. To enforce that transaction is signed using Full Access keys, contracts verify that non-zero deposit was attached. In ft contract, vaa_transfer and vaa_withdraw functions can mint and burn wrapped tokens for any user. If someone was able to obtain FunctionCall key for wormhole AccountId they’d be able to mint any amount of wrapped tokens. So requiring full access keys is a good idea.
candidates.title: Important functions callable with FunctionCall keys

candidates.description: In the byte_utils shared utility code, get_string_from_32 is improperly named and does not enforce a string length of 32 on either the input or output:
candidates.exclusion_note: Status TODO; get_string_from_32 keeps its name on the default branch (near/contracts/wormhole/src/byte_utils.rs), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Byte Util Functions are Improperly Named

candidates.description: There is a controller_or_self function in the Ft template contract:
candidates.exclusion_note: Status TODO; controller_or_self is still present in near/contracts/ft/src/lib.rs on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Dead Code in Ft Contract

candidates.description: In the token-bridge contract, VAA execution happens in two phases via two calls to submit_vaa: 1. In the first step, the VAA is validated and a marker is set in dups referenced by the VAA hash. 2. In the second step, this marker is retrieved by the VAA hash and then the VAA is processed in submit_vaa_work. These checks ensure that the VAA which is processed in the second phase is the same one which was validated in the first phase. However, this check only holds for content which was included in the VAA hash. Importantly, any part of the VAA structure outside of the hashed content (such as the guardian set index) is not included in the hash and therefore not verified in the second step. As a result of this bug, a user can submit an old governance VAA packet by forging the governance_set_index in the second call to submit_vaa.
candidates.exclusion_note: Wormhole stated the behaviour is by design and made no change, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: VAA Header Data can be Forged

candidates.description: Kudelski Security noticed that the token_bridge.py contract contained instances where validated values did not match the allowed values of the Algorand chain. In these cases, the contract rejected any Algorand Standard Assets (ASAs) defined with more than 16 decimal and at the time of this report Algorand Standard Assets (ASAs) can be defined with up to 19 decimals. Additionally, receiveAttest() method, the UnitName was limited to 7, while the max size of a unit name of an asset is 8 bytes on Algorand.
candidates.title: KS-WH-01 – Invalid asset check on ASA

candidates.description: The Kudelski Security team noticed in wormhole_core.py, in the hdlGovernance() method that the smart contract checked the target of the governance message. The function only accepted the value 8 for Algorand or 0 for all chains. (Line 216) Then it checks if the governance message is one of: i) a contract upgrade (lines 220-228) ii) an update of the guardian set (lines 229-267) iii) a message fee, or (lines 268-274) iv) a Payment. (lines 275-293) If the governance is a contract upgrade, the smart contract accepted an upgrade even if the target value was 0.
candidates.title: KS-WH-02 – Missing check for chain on contract upgrade

candidates.description: The Kudelski Security team noticed that the project used multiple instances of the same code and variables. This may have been overlooked due to expansive code or duplicate work. Duplicate code is often a code smell for interesting areas and is used as a metric for code quality for repeatability, standardisation and ease of operation.
candidates.exclusion_note: Status acknowledged; encode_uvarint/get_sig_address are still duplicated in algorand/token_bridge.py and wormhole_core.py on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: KS-WH-03 – Code Duplication

candidates.description: The Kudelski Security team noticed that the pricecaster-v2 project did not implement some best practice checks for transactions. It was noted that the RekeyTo property was not used in transaction objects and not validated. The RekeyTo property specifies the authorized address to transfer ownership of an account to and could be used to authorize future transactions. Similarly the CloseRemainderTo or AssetCloseTo should be set to the intended recipient or equal to global ZeroAddress, to prevent an adversary from performing an unexpected close operation.
candidates.exclusion_note: The fix is in randlabs/pricecaster-v2 (remediation commit f1833d7ec20014bde0876777c53b8213adb73542 named by the report), which the instrument could not clone (git clone asks for credentials: private or removed), so no reachable fix commit can be named.
candidates.title: KS-PC-01 – Missing transaction property checks

candidates.description: It is possible for initializer()-protected functions to be executed twice if this happens in the same transaction. For this to happen, either one call has to be a subcall to the other, or both calls have to be subcalls of a common initializer()-protected function.
candidates.exclusion_note: The response cites PR 1058, but no commit of it is on the default branch and ethereum/package-lock.json still pins @openzeppelin/contracts 4.3.1 (git log -G of package.json/package-lock.json), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Ethereum Bridge: Vulnerable openzeppelin version

candidates.description: Public visibility is used for functions that should be accessible from other contracts, via transactions, and from the current contract. Functions that are not meant to be called internally should have External visibility.
candidates.exclusion_note: Status open; attestToken and completeTransfer are still public in ethereum/contracts/bridge/Bridge.sol on the default branch, so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Ethereum Bridge: Public visibility is set for functions that are not called internally

candidates.description: Some core functionality is not tested for negative scenarios.
candidates.exclusion_note: Status open; no commit adding the listed negative tests could be identified in ethereum/ test history, so no fix commit could be named.
candidates.title: Ethereum Bridge: Uncovered test cases

candidates.description: The local variable is not initialized.
candidates.exclusion_note: Status open; 'uint256 i;' is still uninitialized in Bridge.sol and NFTBridge.sol on the default branch (git log -S), so no fix commit exists.
candidates.title: Ethereum Bridge: Uninitialized local variables

candidates.description: Application does not perform proper input validation and that may lead to nil pointer dereference and instant service crash.
candidates.title: Guardiand: Remote DoS with a single gRPC request

candidates.description: Guardiand commits an observation of events that happened on the blockchain only after some number of blocks are mined on top of the block with event in question, i.e., expects some confirmations. This ensures with high confidence that an observed message will be included into the leading branch of blockchain and inherently persisted in it. This works fine (but never with 100% confidence) for an L1 PoW blockchain. However, for L2 chains that may be not the case. For Polygon, there were cases observed when dead-end branches diverged from others by ~1900 blocks (i. e. had ~1900 blocks at the top differing from the mainline blockchain). Guardiand requires at least a fixed number (512) of confirmations for Polygon network which may cause situations of attestation of message disappeared from mainline blockchain.
candidates.title: Guardiand: Polygon confirmations are not treated properly
